original.target_description: Primary online experiment comparing close personal versus organizational message sources; overall willingness to participate, mediation via cognitive elaboration, and moderation by source credibility. Page 13 contains multiple eligible tests; supplied description does not identify a unique coefficient or hypothesis.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a full 26-page primary research article, with the title Connective-Collective Action on Social Media: Moderated Mediation of Cognitive Elaboration and Perceived Source Credibility on Personalness of Source; authors Elmie Nekmat, Karla K. Gower, Shuhua Zhou, and Miriam Metzger; DOI 10.1177/0093650215609676. These match the original reference. This is the 2015 online-first pagination (1–26), rather than the later volume pagination (62–87). Source PDF path is null, so no PDF was available for layout inspection. Target ambiguity: title-level description and p. 13 locator do not distinguish H1 source effect (printed β = .44, p < .001), covariates (β = .210, p < .001; β = .208, p < .01), RQ1 omnibus/activity-specific tests, or H2 mediation paths (B = .35, p < .01; B = .43, p < .001) and Sobel indirect test (Z = 3.35, p < .01; Table 2 prints Z = 3.351, p = .006). These are candidates only, not selected target statistics. B is explicitly unstandardized in Table 2; no conversion or assumed standardization was performed. N = 208 is printed for the mediation, moderation, and conditional-effects models in Tables 2–4 and for other analyses in Tables 1 and 5. The Method reports personal-source n = 102 and organizational-source n = 106, but these are assignment counts, not explicitly final post-exclusion groups for an identified critical test; no analytic N sum was adopted. Common model N = 208 is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review while row correspondence remains unresolved. Unassigned fields and replication/success are null placeholders, not assessments of unavailable primary sources.
